reasoning: Every class holds: the baseline is standard hooks at the publisher's own pins with no new script, each scenario has a test, the RED group names only ids that are red, every tool behaviour the design rests on was observed live — including the unquoted-args defect and both mypy probes — and the last replaced input, the installation PR's own gate, is now listed in D5 with the repository's remedy and stated in Install step 1 before `--confirm`.

simpler.evidence: The baseline is standard hook repositories at the publisher's own pins, written outside the marker block by the existing create-once path (design D1, D2; proposal Why on `_block_text`), so the change adds no installer mechanism and no script. The simpler options are recorded and rejected against the scenarios: hooks inside the block (every upgrade rewrites them, D1), merging into an existing config (forbidden by `Init fails closed on inputs it does not own`, D1), the mypy hook's default args (the silent `Any`, D2 with the live probe), `language: system` (the alias pre-commit will deprecate, D2), mypy in the project environment or at the `manual` stage only (D2), seeding whenever the declaration is absent (a `test` that runs none of the baseline, D4), and pre-commit run from the quality callee or `quality.py` (a second implicit source of the gate's command, D4).

map.evidence: Nine scenarios across the two MODIFIED and one ADDED requirement, each with an entry in tasks.md's scenario → test map (lines 47-55); the four pre-existing scenarios keep their tests and 1.4 lists them among the green-by-design guards. Both revised behaviours ride scenarios that already exist rather than adding any: `Created config` carries the `args: []` clause, asserted by 1.2 (`mypy`'s `args == []`), and `Fresh install seeds the declaration` carries the seeded `setup`, asserted by 1.1 against the declaration written verbatim in design D4, with the `pre-commit` and `pytest` pins read from `.agent-process/requirements-dev.txt` so the test and D3 stay in one place. The established-repository case added to D5 is a consequence of requirements already specified (a created config carries the baseline; the run seeds the declaration), not a new behaviour, so it rightly adds no scenario.

red.evidence: Task 1.4 runs `check_red` on nine quoted parametrized node ids and names what fails in each body; the ids were confirmed against collection (`[scenario-mode-platform]`), and the cases that are green by design — `test_quality_command_marker[existing-config]`, the `upgrade` parametrizations of `test_lifecycle` that return early, `test_existing_config_keeps_its_hooks`, the loosened block test — are listed as guards rather than passed to `check_red`, which refuses a report with a green case. The revisions added no test and none was needed: `args: []` is asserted inside `test_created_config_carries_the_baseline` and the seeded `setup` inside `test_quality_command_marker[fresh]`, both already in the RED set and both red before groups 2-3 (no baseline hook to parse, no declaration written); the D5/D6 documentation of group 4 is prose the plan explicitly marks as untested.

platform.evidence: Every behaviour the plan rests on was observed, not asserted (proposal Why): the `mypy` hook with `args: []` failing `Library stubs not installed for "requests" [import-untyped]` and then, with `additional_dependencies: [types-requests]`, `"Response" has no attribute "json_data"`, beside mypy's documentation, the Scientific Python guide and `psf/black`'s config; the `for f in ...; do if [ -f "$f" ]; ... || exit 1; fi; done` loop under `bash -e -c 'eval ...'` exiting 0 with neither lockfile and 1 on a failed install, matched to `run: eval "$SETUP"` on `ubuntu-latest` in `.github/workflows/quality.yml` (the `check` job runs `setup` only when it is non-empty; the pre-push hook runs only `test`); pre-commit 4.6.0's stage and `Skipped` semantics; `--extend-select` keeping a repository's own selection; the unquoted-args YAML defect the live run caught; pylint `C0302 (1005/1000)`; the 73 s cold install against ADR 0034's 120 s timeout; and `language: unsupported` from the 4.4.0 CHANGELOG. The rendering behaviour is now applied to both templates: `init._template` calls `string.Template(text).substitute(values)` even with no values (`init.py:177-179`; `_template("dependabot.yml")` at 484), and task 3.1 writes each `$f` of the seeded `setup` as `$$f`, as 2.1 does for the pre-commit template's regexes. Asserted-minor, accepted: what an older pre-commit prints for `minimum_pre_commit_version`.

replaced.evidence: Design D5 now lists every replaced input with the step its failure reaches: the lost `check_red` proof, caught by the baseline `pytest` hook once a test file is tracked; packages outside both lockfiles (this revision replaced the old "installs only pre-commit" mode — `setup` installs each lockfile that exists); a redefined `python_files` (accepted, routed to ADR 0035 and PR body 6.2); a narrowed config with no `manual` hook left; and the one I raised — a repository with its own code and no `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has its installation PR's `agent-process / quality` run the baseline over pre-adoption code and fail before `activate_protection`, with the remedy being its own commit on that PR under D1's ownership, stated in Install step 1 before `--confirm` (D6, task 4.1) and recorded in ADR 0035. The Migration Plan's trigger is now the created config rather than a fresh repository, which is what `init` actually keys on. D2 lists what `args: []` replaces (the hook's default args) and the `additional_dependencies`-versus-requirements drift that remains.

catcher.evidence: Each catcher traces to a delivery step: the baseline `pytest` hook inside the seeded `test` reaches `agent-process / quality` on the first-tests PR's head and the pre-push hook on the same push; a package outside both lockfiles reaches that PR's `check` job as `No module named ...` (the pre-push hook runs only `test`, so the pusher's own environment supplies the deps — the same visible failure one step earlier); a stub-less import reaches the committer at edit time with mypy's own fix-naming message; the baseline over pre-adoption code reaches the person on the installation PR, now with the remedy they read in Install step 1; `pytest...Skipped` under a redefined `python_files` reaches only the gate's log, which is why it stays an accepted gap in the PR body (6.2). On the publisher side, 1.1 and 1.2 catch a wrong pin, a wrong arg string or a template that fails to render at group 3's verify command, before any release.

length.evidence: The modified requirement adds ~40 words about the seeded `setup` and the `unchanged` transition; both are asserted word-for-word — the `setup` by 1.1 (equality with D4's literal declaration, pins from `.agent-process/requirements-dev.txt`) and the transition by 1.1's `malformed`/`declared` cases plus `quality` in `LABELS` (1.3). The ADDED requirement's new clause is ~13 words (`mypy` of `pre-commit/mirrors-mypy` with `args: []`, so an import it cannot resolve fails the hook), asserted by 1.2's `args == []` and exercised live in 5.3. The footprint requirement grows by one path and one word ("eight files"), asserted by `CONSUMER_FILES` in 1.3. The only unasserted new text is the group 4 documentation: ADR 0035 and the ~20 words Install step 1 gains about the established-repository case, which cannot be tested — it describes a consumer's own repository state — and task 4.1 says so instead of inventing a check; the existing doc-structure tests still run over both files.

bespoke.evidence: The plan adds no script and no check of its own — design D2 closes with it, and every tool is a published hook repository at the publisher's pin. The two non-standard pieces carry their decision: the `local` `pytest` hook exists because pytest publishes no pre-commit hook (D2) and leans on pytest's own configuration rather than a wrapper, and `pylint` runs with `--disable=all --enable=too-many-lines` because ruff has no module-length rule (ADR 0028). The new installer code is one `quality` entry in the existing `_consumer_steps`/`_file_step` mechanism plus a template file, not a new deterministic check.
